answers.q1_what_did_you_play: Nereid's Ascension first, for 16 to all three enemies plus whatever Charge 8 adds. That alone kills Twig Slime (S) at 10 HP and Leaf Slime (S) at 15 HP outright, and takes Leaf Slime (M) from 32 down to 16 or lower. Then Water's Edge on whatever the board still shows alive after the sweep — Leaf Slime (M) if the two smalls are already dead, which is what I expect. That leaves 0 energy spent on Block and one Water's Edge, three Coral Guards, a Bake-Kurage and All Streams still in hand. The reasoning: the whole incoming attack on the board is 4 damage from Twig Slime (S), and the sweep kills that enemy before it swings. The other two intents are status cards, which Block does nothing about. So Block this turn buys almost nothing, and killing bodies is the only thing that removes damage — this turn and every later turn. Two dead enemies is the largest permanent reduction available, and Nereid's Ascension is the only card that gets both in one action.
answers.q2_other_line_considered: Yes — the line that skips the AoE entirely: Water's Edge on Twig Slime (S) is not enough on its own (6 vs 10 HP), so it would be All Streams Flow to the Sea plus Water's Edge to kill Twig Slime, plus a Coral Guard, spending all 3 energy to eat the 4-damage attack and hold Nereid's Ascension for a bigger board later. I weighed it because Nereid's Ascension exhausts — playing it here spends a one-shot card on 10 and 15 HP slimes, and the elite or boss room is where a 16-to-all is worth most. I rejected it because both status-card intents resolve regardless of what I do, so the Leaf Slimes keep polluting my deck every turn they live, and the only counter to that is speed. The single-target line kills one body and leaves 47 HP of enemy plus two more status cards arriving. The sweep kills two bodies and cuts the third in half. Also considered folding Bake-Kurage in for the Charge before the sweep, but Nereid's Ascension is 2 and Bake-Kurage is 1, which is exactly 3, and I would rather have the guaranteed Water's Edge finish than one extra Charge on an AoE that already kills everything it needs to kill.
answers.q3_what_it_gave_up: The exhaust card, permanently — Nereid's Ascension is gone from the deck for the rest of the run, spent on a three-slime encounter rather than saved for a room where 16-to-all matters more. It also gave up all Block: I take whatever the live board actually swings if the intents differ from what is telegraphed here, and I have no defense up despite holding three Coral Guards. And it gave up the Bake-Kurage summon and the Charge it would have built, which would have made every later Charge-scaling card in the deck hit harder. I am trading long-run resources for ending this fight two turns sooner and eating fewer status cards.
answers.q4_different_intent: Yes. The intents are what made this easy, and two changes would flip it. If Leaf Slime (M) were telegraphing a large attack instead of status cards — say 15 or more — then Block starts mattering and I would look at Shinobu - Sanctifying Circle for the 4 Block plus chip, or spend the spare energy on Coral Guard instead of the second Water's Edge. If all three enemies were telegraphing attacks totaling something my 48 HP could not comfortably absorb, I would still lead Nereid's Ascension (killing attackers is the best block) but the leftover energy goes to Coral Guard, not Water's Edge. Conversely, if every enemy were telegraphing status or a buff and nothing was attacking at all, I would consider the greedy line — Bake-Kurage for Charge, then All Streams — and hold Nereid's Ascension for later, since nothing punishes a slow turn. What did not move me: the exact numbers on the status intents. Two cards versus one changes nothing about which enemy I want dead.
